genericProblem: A module-relocation integration-test proof can be invalidated either by a stale filesystem Flyway location or by an assertion that reads shared class-level database state rather than the scenario's own row set.

counterexamples.reason: Production migration configuration uses classpath:db/migration and is outside the filesystem test-location denominator.
This test uses classpath migration discovery, not a module-relative filesystem location.
The Test task has no workingDir override; each affected module project directory remains the resolution base.

findings.finding: All eight active filesystem Flyway test locations retain the obsolete ../../../ prefix after the P2 module relocation; the old resolved root is absent and ../../src/main/resources/db/migration is the unique existing application migration root relative to every module project directory.
The former static-only P2 evidence binding did not require a test execution and existing Flyway layout controls did not resolve test filesystem locations, so this runtime-path class was unproved.

WorkspaceInvitationPublicFlowTest reused one class-level database and asserted a global role_assignment count, so a prior test's completed invitation made later zero-assignment scenarios order-dependent. The finite counterexample is this one test class; all seven other Flyway filesystem tests completed in their suites without this signal.

preventionDispositions.reason: A finite live-source resolver denominator and red mutation will reject an obsolete module-relative prefix before package exit.
The P2 technical-relocation binding will require current-byte dynamic evidence while preserving NOT_APPLICABLE for unchanged end-user behavior.
For Testcontainers classes with multiple scenarios, review assertions that count mutable rows to ensure they bind to the current scenario identity rather than a class-global residue.
